headline.technical: Financial Times reported Big Tech shed nearly $900bn over AI spending; Nasdaq Composite closed 1d -1.38% while KOSPI fell 1d -3.48% and Nikkei 225 1d -2.12%.
headline.layman: Big tech firms are spending huge sums on AI and investors got nervous, so tech shares fell worldwide, with Asian chip-heavy markets hit hardest.

status.technical: The Financial Times reported Big Tech shed nearly $900bn as cash burn at Google, Amazon and Meta led Wall Street to question the price of the AI boom. Nasdaq Composite closed 1d -1.38%; KOSPI 1d -3.48% and TAIEX 1d -2.49% on 2026-10-30.
status.layman: The Financial Times reported big tech firms lost nearly $900bn in value as investors question how much they spend on AI. Tech shares in Asia fell sharply too.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported hyperscalers keep spending big on AI, pressuring legacy businesses and free cash flow. If spending keeps outrunning returns, tech valuations may stay under pressure.
consequence.layman: CNBC says the big tech firms are spending heavily on AI, which strains their older businesses and cash. If that continues, tech shares may stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Asian chipmakers were hit: Straits Times reported Singapore chip stocks tumbled, and among Nikkei names Tokyo Electron fell -5.19% (1d) and SK Hynix -7.08% (1d) in KOSPI. Evidence on non-tech sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Chip-related shares in Asia fell most. Tokyo Electron dropped -5.19% in a day and SK Hynix -7.08%. The notes say little about other sectors.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, next day rose 50% of 169 times and next 5 days rose 54% of 169 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after similar Nasdaq drops it rose the next day 50% of 169 times and over the next 5 days 54% of 169 times.

status.technical: Wall Street closed 2026-10-29 with S&P 500 1d -0.30% and Nasdaq Composite 1d -1.38%, while Russell 2000 gained 1d 1.01%. CNBC reported Amazon fell 7% and Intel plunged 25% in premarket trading after earnings.
status.layman: US stocks slipped Thursday, tech most, while smaller companies rose. CNBC reported Amazon was down 7% and Intel 25% before Friday's open after their results.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported investors are reassessing AI valuations and capital expenditure. If that continues, tech-heavy indices could stay under pressure.
consequence.layman: Investors are rethinking how much AI is worth. If doubts continue, tech-heavy markets could stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Large tech holders are most exposed: among the largest S&P 500 names Alphabet was -12.64% (1d) and Amazon -4.25% (1d). CNBC reported investors are preparing for Democratic gains in the midterm election on Tuesday.
impact.layman: People holding big tech shares feel it most: Alphabet fell -12.64% in a day. CNBC says investors are also preparing for Tuesday's US midterm election.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500's next day rose 54% of 845 times and next 5 days rose 59% of 842 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 845 times and over 5 days 59% of 842 times.

status.technical: Euro zone growth slowed to 0.4% in Q3 (CNBC) while France shrank 0.1% (FT). Euro Stoxx 50 closed 1d -0.81% and DAX 1d -0.58%, while FTSE 100 rose 1d 0.26% as oil prices approached six-month highs (Yahoo Finance).
status.layman: Europe's economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter but France shrank 0.1%. Most European stocks fell, while London's FTSE 100 rose.

consequence.technical: WSJ reported French debt worries are mounting amid political paralysis, and Bloomberg said this weighs on the euro. If concerns persist, French assets may remain under pressure.
consequence.layman: WSJ says worries about France's debt are growing. If they continue, the euro and French assets may stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Economic Times said European blue-chips are set for their strongest earnings in four years, driven by energy profits, while automakers' recovery is fragile amid Chinese competition.
impact.layman: Energy firms are lifting European company profits, but carmakers still face tough competition from China.

status.technical: KOSPI closed 1d -3.48%, TAIEX 1d -2.49% and Nikkei 225 1d -2.12% as Economic Times and Bloomberg tied losses to the global AI selloff hitting chipmakers; Hang Seng rose 1d 1.46% and Nifty 50 1d 0.51%.
status.layman: Chip-heavy markets in South Korea, Taiwan and Japan fell most as AI worries spread. Hong Kong and India rose.

consequence.layman: Foreign investors pulled money out of South Korea. If chip selling continues, these markets stay exposed.

impact.layman: Taiwan's economy is booming, with 14.36% growth, yet its stocks fell. China's main index hit a one-year low after 12 weeks of losses.

status.layman: Amazon and Intel's results made investors worry about the cost of building AI and whether it will pay off.

consequence.technical: If AI capex keeps rising ahead of returns, CNBC reported legacy businesses and free cash flow of hyperscalers come under pressure.

impact.technical: Tech shares and chipmakers across Asia and the US are affected; Foxconn said there is no AI bubble (Straits Times).

drivers.title: Oil, Iran war and energy profits

status.technical: Al Jazeera reported Brent crude prices are up more than 60 percent versus pre-war levels despite a rebound in supply. Brent closed 113.62 (1d -1.10%). Bloomberg reported Exxon and Chevron beat profit expectations as refining results hit record highs.
status.layman: Oil prices are far above pre-war levels, Al Jazeera reported. US oil giants Exxon and Chevron beat profit expectations on refining.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported European energy companies are expected to post a striking increase in profits from higher oil prices. Economic Times said Indian shares turned lower when crude crossed $116 per barrel on inflation and growth concerns.
consequence.layman: High oil prices lift energy company profits, but Economic Times says they worry Indian investors about inflation and growth.

impact.technical: Oil majors gain; BP's third-quarter profit nearly quadrupled to $8.5 billion (CNBC). Oil importers such as India face inflation concerns per Economic Times.
impact.layman: Oil companies are earning more, for example BP at $8.5 billion. Countries that buy oil, like India, worry about higher prices.

status.layman: Japan's central bank kept its rate at 1.25% but signalled hikes. UK firms expect prices to rise 3.8%, up from 3.7%. US borrowing costs eased.

consequence.layman: Reuters says the ECB's survey expects higher inflation. If prices keep rising faster, central banks have less room to cut rates.
